court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Civil Judge Senior Division at Vaduj, Satara
case_name: Harshada Omkar Dahiwadikar vs Omkar Sanad Dahiwadikar
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties are the wife and husband who were married in 2019. The wife claims harassment, torture, and insult by the husband's family members for more dowry. She has been residing with her parents since March 2020. The husband filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, for restitution of conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: The ends of justice would be served if the Marriage Petition is transferred to the Court where the Divorce Petition is pending.
legal_principles.held: Having heard the learned Counsel and having perused the Application and considering the inconvenience and hardship of the wife as narrated above, this Court is of the view that ends of justice would be served if the Marriage Petition No.124 of 2020 filed by the Respondent-husband before the Civil Judge Senior Division, Vaduj, Satara, is transferred to the Court of
cited_cases: Harshada Omkar Dahiwadikar vs Omkar Sanad Dahiwadikar on 27 September, 2023

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking transfer to show that it would be in the interests of justice.
legal_principles.held: He would submit that, in any case, the Divorce Petition has been filed by the Applicant-wife in Vasai, and therefore, it would be in the interests of justice if the Petition for restitution of conjugal rights is transferred to the same Court where the Divorce Petition is pending.
cited_cases: Harshada Omkar Dahiwadikar vs Omkar Sanad Dahiwadikar on 27 September, 2023

outcome.final_order: The proceedings for restitution of conjugal rights are transferred to this court from the trial court.
